searchText: For the record, deposit-cli installed and worked fine on MacOS once I used a virtualenv so it wasn't trying to install to a system folder. I assume I could have also installed it with `sudo` but that didn't seem like a great idea. My experience registering a validator with LaunchPad was very good overall and I'm really keen to see an instance up and running for Medalla. Hey guys, the launchpad site is shaping up very nicely. However, didn't have a very positive experience once I had to reach the page that asked the user to install python 3.7 + and the deposit util. Will there be one-click binaries we can just download and run instead? From our experience with operating the Onyx testnet, this will turn-off a huge amount of users, likely over half of the people trying the launchpad, if there are no simple binaries to run Some of our teammates also had issues with the installation steps (Sorry I’m afk today, quickly replying here) There is a `venv` quick start command: `make venv_deposit` for the virtualenv users. I think the idea of installing from source code was for making sure the source is legit (from GitHub though) <@550420431744794624> ? But I agreed with <@311971895828283393> that it’s not the best for user experience... <@340345049063882753> I also saw the `sudo` solution and also don’t think it’s good for installing a crypto tool with sudo. 😢 Three solutions I see: 1. Convert it to binaries 2. Use virtualenv, but it requires user to know some venv troubleshooting knowledge if they stuck 3. Add sudo to the script 😓 Personally I'd say have a binary option available for users who are happy to trust it, and that then gives some leeway to have the compile from source instructions a little more complex using venv. > Personally I'd say have a binary option available for users who are happy to trust it How about signing binaries and providing checksum instead of trusting blindly 😅 Signing the binaries only works if the user trusts the PK. Eg. Prysm's signing is cool, but it has the same chicken and egg problem with the PK I think most users trust PK used for signing geth binaries (from build server) Most users are happy to trust a binary download yes. Some will actually check the signature (more should) and a very few will actually verify the signature against a known good source (rather than happily accepting a hackers signature). But the real point is that users can make that choice themselves. I'm a bit torn here. being able to get something running on the command line is almost the bare minimum requirement we're willing to accept for technical competency for running a validator some % drop-off there isn't necessarily a bad thing it's not about running something on the command-line but rather untangling python's not so optimal way of managing dependencies and installing binaries. I will personally rather use the tooling provided by the clients than the python deposit helper, this does not necessarily mean, I don't know how to use the command line downloading a binary seems the best option here, you still would have to use the command line. you can even add a checksum check to the launchpad instructions and tell users to abort in case it fails maybe it alao openly lists alternatives such as the prysm or lighthouse launchpads or points to furrher documentation for "advanced" users so in case people have issues the the cli, they can be assisted in finding alternatives we just launched https://beaconcha.in/poap and linked the discord channels for all clients in the table at the bottom so new users can enter the community more easily 😇 Nice! What do we use to prevent the same validator uses all 5 graffitis? nothing, it’s gamable, there are generally no incentives on a testnet :/ Maybe filter graffiti coming from the same validator? Not perfect but it will prevent the obvious attack yeah, the script should def just use the 0th graffiti from a given validator don't want to double count vals anyway. could end up with more poaps than vals if so! > Maybe filter graffiti coming from the same validator? Not perfect but it will prevent the obvious attack we have some ideas but i don't it's wise to share them here 😄 > The tokens will be distributed via a mechanism called a merkle drop. This is like an airdrop, but badges are only distributed to those who actively claim them reducing state bloat and chain congestion. > > This is like an airdrop, but badges are only distributed to those who actively claim them, reducing state bloat and chain congestion. excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: For the record, deposit-cli installed and worked fine on MacOS once I used a virtualenv so it wasn't trying to install to a system folder. I assume I could have also installed it with `sudo` but that didn't seem like a great idea. My experience registering a validator with LaunchPad was very good overall and I'm really keen to see an instance up and running for Medalla.

excerpts.author: raulj
excerpts.content: Hey guys, the launchpad site is shaping up very nicely. However, didn't have a very positive experience once I had to reach the page that asked the user to install python 3.7 + and the deposit util. Will there be one-click binaries we can just download and run instead? From our experience with operating the Onyx testnet, this will turn-off a huge amount of users, likely over half of the people trying the launchpad, if there are no simple binaries to run

excerpts.author: raulj
excerpts.content: Some of our teammates also had issues with the installation steps

excerpts.author: hsiaowei
excerpts.content:
(Sorry I’m afk today, quickly replying here)

There is a `venv` quick start command:
`make venv_deposit` for the virtualenv users.

I think the idea of installing from source code was for making sure the source is legit (from GitHub though) <@550420431744794624> ? But I agreed with <@311971895828283393> that it’s not the best for user experience... 

<@340345049063882753> I also saw the `sudo` solution and also don’t think it’s good for installing a crypto tool with sudo. 😢

Three solutions I see:
1. Convert it to binaries 
2. Use virtualenv, but it requires user to know some venv troubleshooting knowledge if they stuck
3. Add sudo to the script 😓

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Personally I'd say have a binary option available for users who are happy to trust it, and that then gives some leeway to have the compile from source instructions a little more complex using venv.

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content:
> Personally I'd say have a binary option available for users who are happy to trust it
How about signing binaries and providing checksum instead of trusting blindly 😅

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content: Signing the binaries only works if the user trusts the PK. Eg. Prysm's signing is cool, but it has the same chicken and egg problem with the PK

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content: I think most users trust PK used for signing geth binaries (from build server)

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Most users are happy to trust a binary download yes. Some will actually check the signature (more should) and a very few will actually verify the signature against a known good source (rather than happily accepting a hackers signature). But the real point is that users can make that choice themselves.
